chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Thelonious Monk: respect from afar
summary: Horace never saw Monk play but respects him as a creator from what musicians say.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Well, the thing is that with people like Dizzy and Bird and various people involved that, even if the musicians didn't like the style, they had to admit that these guys could play their horns, you know.
Yeah. What about somebody like Thelonius Monk, whose style was just somewhere else, compared to what had been going on in piano playing? How did you feel about that?

Unfortunately, I don't know too much about Thelonius Monk, except I've read a little something about him, and I've never seen him play. I've heard one or two of his recordings, but they were interesting, and I've heard musicians that play in my group talk about him. And they respected him, you know, and they said, he knows what he's doing, you know. I would love to have met him, you know, because he created something there, Thelonius Monk.
So in my book, just from what I've
heard the guys say, the little that I've read, he's a legend.
